Introduction 
This document discusses IIN information for the following card types: 
• American Express 
• Debit 
• Diners Club 
• Discover Network 
• EBT 
• Fleet One 
• Fleetwide 
• Fuelman 
• JCB 
• MasterCard 
• MasterCard Fleet 
• Visa 
• Visa Fleet 
• Voyager 
• WEX 
This document contains two tables. 
• Table 1 contains the following information: 
o Card Type 
o Card Type ID 
o IIN Length 
o PAN Length 
o PAN Range—Low 
o PAN Range—High 
• Table 2 contains the following information: 
o Card Type 
o Manual Entry

Support of 8-Digit BIN: Effective with the April 2022 release, Visa, MasterCard, and Discover will implement the change from six-digit 
to eight-digit issuing BINs to align with the new standard adopted by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). 
Acquirers and processors must be able to support both 6-digit and 8-digit issuing BINs by April 2022. Issuers must be able to support 
eight-digit issuing BINs for new BINs requested after April 2022. First Data Acquiring platforms have been updated to support this 
mandate. In addition, the First Data Global BIN File has been updated to recognize Issuer BIN lengths greater than six digits. To 
ensure readiness, First Data recommends all partners carefully review these changes to identify any impacts and pay particular 
attention to any processes that utilize BIN information for processing purposes, such as Merchant Choice Routing, Merchant Loyalty 
(special discount programs offered to cardholders who execute “on us” transactions), Dual Branded BIN lists for mag-stripe 
transactions, and PIN bypass eligibility for mag-stripe transactions. Integrated Partners should ensure that their systems are able to 
properly handle these changes or incorporate the necessary action plans to achieve compliance by April 2022.

Card Type Information—Table 2 
The following table lists each card type in alphabetical order, together with the following 
information: 
• Manual Entry—Indicates whether manual entry can be used. 
• Encrypted PIN Required—If a PIN (personal identification number) is entered, and this 
column contains a Y for the card, the PIN must be encrypted. 
• IIN Entered—If manual entry for a card is supported, and the column contains a Y for the 
card, then no special processing is required to determine the IIN.  If the column contains an 
N for the card, then special processing is required to verify the card number and append the 
IIN.
